The model reads "_n_ is a |X|" through the unit chain (decisions.md, child-of-through-unit-chain), so its literal reading passes step 1 and stops (a sort error) at step 2, where _n_'s production has no |X|. alts.text: It is a Syntax Error if the StringValue of |IdentifierName| is the String value of any terminal of |ReservedWord| except for `yield` or `await`.
It is a Syntax Error if the StringValue of |IdentifierName| is the String value of any terminal of |ReservedWord| except for `yield` or `await`.

notes: "the StringValue of any |ReservedWord| except for `yield` or `await`" takes the StringValue of a |ReservedWord|, for which StringValue has no row. The literal text stops there. The test262 and proposed reading: the StringValue of a terminal is the String value of its code points (test262's val-*-via-escape-*.js require a SyntaxError for an |IdentifierName| that spells a reserved word with escapes).

A lookahead restriction reads "the immediately following input token sequence" (§5.1.6.7), and §12.10 inserts semicolons "into the source code token stream": the text does not say whether an inserted semicolon is a token a lookahead reads. Read as one, `if (0) let` LF `[a] = 0;` is a sentence. The literal text stops wherever a lookahead reads at an inserted semicolon. The test262 and proposed reading: a lookahead reads the source's tokens, past the semicolons §12.10 inserted (test262's let-array-with-newline.js require a SyntaxError).

B.1.1 adds |HTMLCloseComment| as an alternative of |InputElementHashbangOrRegExp| of its own, not under |Comment|, and §5.1.3 drops only white space and comments from the input elements: literally a first-line `-->` is a token that no syntactic production has, and the |Script| has no parse (a SyntaxError). The test262 and proposed reading: an |HTMLCloseComment| input element is a comment (test262's single-line-html-close-first-line-{1,2,3}.js).

B.1.2's "each alternative is considered only if previous production alternatives do not match" says neither what an alternative matches nor how nested choices combine, and without an order its grammar is ambiguous (`/a{1}/`, `/\b*/`, `/\1/`). The literal text stops on a pattern with more than one parse. The test262 and proposed reading: commitment: a node of a nonterminal B.1.2 restates uses an alternative only if no earlier alternative of it derives any span from the node's start (tc39/ecma262 #2228; test262's annexB/built-ins/RegExp).

B.1.2's condition on `AtomEscape :: DecimalEscape`, "the CapturingGroupNumber of |DecimalEscape| is ≤ CountLeftCapturingParensWithin(the |Pattern| containing |DecimalEscape|)", reads the |Pattern| whose parse the condition itself decides. The literal text stops on a pattern with more than one parse. The test262 and proposed reading: stratified: the count is that of a committed parse of the input as Pattern[~UnicodeMode, ~UnicodeSetsMode, ~NamedCaptureGroups] with the condition true (test262's legacy-octal-escape.js).

notes: _now_ is read after DoWait's reading from which [[TimeoutTime]] was computed, so the literal difference is negative when the clock has advanced past [[TimeoutTime]], and HostEnqueueTimeoutJob takes a non-negative finite Number. The proposed reading clamps the text's own difference at zero, so that _now_ + _delay_ is 𝔽([[TimeoutTime]]) whenever the delay is positive: the Job runs no earlier than that time value, which is what AtomicsWaitAsyncTimeoutAssert's proposed Assert needs. Clamping the exact difference instead (𝔽(max([[TimeoutTime]] - ℝ(_now_), 0))) can round the delay down across a millisecond that 𝔽([[TimeoutTime]]) rounds up to.

While SpecTec keeps the literal subtraction at EnqueueAtomicsWaitAsyncTimeoutJob step 4, runtime parameter-sort checks are omitted and Engine.Host.Strategy.msCeil clamps negative timeout delays up to 0 ms (and wakeFinite in 16-host-laws-jobs.spectec caps finite agent suspension timeouts at maxTime = 8.64 × 10^15 ms).

Step 1.a of Races (sec-races) is always true: an execution's happens-before is a strict partial order, so _eventA_ and _eventB_ never both happen-before each other, and any two conflicting events race. The memory model's meaning (Ecma.MemoryModel.Race) reads the literal text. The proposed text of step 1.a: "If neither _eventA_ happens-before _eventB_ in _execution_ nor _eventB_ happens-before _eventA_ in _execution_, then".

The third condition of happens-before orders an ~init~ write only before events whose memory ranges are *overlapping*, and "overlapping" excludes equal ranges, so a 1-byte event at an ~init~ event's byte is not ordered after it. The proposed text: "SharedDataBlockEventSet(_execution_) contains both _eventA_ and _eventB_, _eventA_.[[Order]] is ~init~, _eventA_ and _eventB_ are not the same Shared Data Block event, and _eventA_ and _eventB_ do not have disjoint memory ranges."

A memory range is a Set of integers, the byte indices from [[ByteIndex]], with no [[Block]] in it, so reads-bytes-from's "has _readEvent_.[[ByteIndex]] + _i_ in its memory range" and coherent reads' "has _byteLocation_ in its memory range" (step 1.c.ii) admit a write to another Shared Data Block at the same index. The proposed text, which the memory model's meaning (Ecma.MemoryModel.Rbf.Valid, CoherentReads) reads: "Each event _writeEvent_ with index _i_ in _writes_ has _readEvent_.[[Block]] as its [[Block]] and _readEvent_.[[ByteIndex]] + _i_ in its memory range", and in step 1.c.ii "a WriteSharedMemory or ReadModifyWriteSharedMemory event _value_ whose [[Block]] is _readEvent_.[[Block]] and that has _byteLocation_ in its memory range".

1. Let _entries_ be IntrinsicObjects().

        1. For each Record _entry_ of _entries_, do

          1. If _entry_.[[Behaviour]] is not ~empty~, then
            1. If _entry_.[[Prefix]] is ~empty~, let _obj_ be CreateBuiltinFunction(_entry_.[[Behaviour]], _entry_.[[Length]], _entry_.[[Name]], _entry_.[[Slots]], _realmRecord_, _proto_); else let _obj_ be CreateBuiltinFunction(_entry_.[[Behaviour]], _entry_.[[Length]], _entry_.[[Name]], _entry_.[[Slots]], _realmRecord_, _proto_, _entry_.[[Prefix]]).
            1. Set _obj_.[[Async]] to _entry_.[[Async]].
            1. If _entry_.[[Constructor]] is *true*, set _obj_.[[Construct]] to the definition specified in <emu-xref href="#sec-built-in-function-objects-construct-argumentslist-newtarget"></emu-xref>.
          1. Else,
            1. Let _obj_ be OrdinaryObjectCreate(_proto_, _entry_.[[Slots]]).
            1. If _entry_.[[Exotic]] is <emu-xref href="#sec-array-exotic-objects"></emu-xref>, then
              1. Set _obj_.[[DefineOwnProperty]] as specified in <emu-xref href="#sec-array-exotic-objects-defineownproperty-p-desc"></emu-xref>.
            1. Else if _entry_.[[Exotic]] is <emu-xref href="#sec-string-exotic-objects"></emu-xref>, then
              1. Set _obj_.[[GetOwnProperty]] as specified in <emu-xref href="#sec-string-exotic-objects-getownproperty-p"></emu-xref>.
              1. Set _obj_.[[DefineOwnProperty]] as specified in <emu-xref href="#sec-string-exotic-objects-defineownproperty-p-desc"></emu-xref>.
              1. Set _obj_.[[OwnPropertyKeys]] as specified in <emu-xref href="#sec-string-exotic-objects-ownpropertykeys"></emu-xref>.
            1. Else if _entry_.[[Exotic]] is <emu-xref href="#sec-immutable-prototype-exotic-objects"></emu-xref>, then
              1. Set _obj_.[[SetPrototypeOf]] to the definition specified in <emu-xref href="#sec-immutable-prototype-exotic-objects-setprototypeof-v"></emu-xref>.
          1. For each Record _slot_ of _entry_.[[SlotValues]], do
            1. Perform SetFieldNamed(_obj_, _slot_.[[Name]], _slot_.[[Value]]).
          1. For each element _name_ of _entry_.[[Names]], do
            1. Perform SetFieldNamed(_realmRecord_.[[Intrinsics]], _name_, _obj_).
          1. Append _obj_ to _objects_.
        1. For each Record _entry_ of _entries_, do
          1. Let _obj_ be _objects_[_entry_.[[Index]]].
          1. If _entry_.[[Behaviour]] is not ~empty~, then
            1. Let _la_ be _entry_.[[LengthAttributes]].
            1. Perform ! DefinePropertyOrThrow(_obj_, *"length"*, PropertyDescriptor { [[Writable]]: _la_.[[Writable]], [[Enumerable]]: _la_.[[Enumerable]], [[Configurable]]: _la_.[[Configurable]] }).
            1. Let _na_ be _entry_.[[NameAttributes]].
            1. Perform ! DefinePropertyOrThrow(_obj_, *"name"*, PropertyDescriptor { [[Writable]]: _na_.[[Writable]], [[Enumerable]]: _na_.[[Enumerable]], [[Configurable]]: _na_.[[Configurable]] }).
          1. For each Record _p_ of PropertyOrder(_obj_, _entry_.[[Properties]]), do
            1. If PropertyProvided(_p_) is *true*, perform OwnPropertyCreate(_obj_, _p_.[[Key]], IntrinsicPropertyDescriptor(_p_, _objects_), _p_.[[Kind]]).
          1. Set _obj_.[[Extensible]] to _entry_.[[Extensible]].

notes: Step 2 creates each built-in function by "CreateBuiltinFunction(_steps_, _length_, _name_, _slots_, _realmRecord_, _proto_, _async_)", which passes _async_ as CreateBuiltinFunction's _prefix_ and gives no accessor its prefix; read literally, SetFunctionName concatenates a Boolean and realm creation stops. test262 requires both: built-ins/Array/fromAsync/ (an async function) and built-ins/Map/prototype/size/name.js (*"get size"*). The proposed text: "CreateBuiltinFunction(_steps_, _length_, _name_, _slots_, _realmRecord_, _proto_, _prefix_, _async_), where _prefix_ is *"get"* or *"set"* for a get or set accessor function of a built-in property and ~empty~ otherwise", with an ~empty~ _prefix_ read as not present.

1. Let _next_ be SortStep(the number of elements in _items_, ~empty~, ~empty~).
        1. Repeat, while _next_ is a List,
          1. Let _result_ be _sortCompare_(_items_[_next_[0]], _items_[_next_[1]]).
          1. If _result_ is an abrupt completion, return _result_.
          1. Set _next_ to SortStep(the number of elements in _items_, _next_[2], _result_).
        1. Let _sorted_ be a new empty List.

notes: The definition of a consistent comparator reads each result as ℝ(_comparator_(_a_, _b_)), which has no value for ±∞; the literal reading stops there. No test262 test has a comparator return ±∞. The test262 reading has no ℝ step: by SortStep's law no consistent comparator gives a ±∞ result, so the order is the host's, and both test hosts order by the result's sign. The proposed text compares the Number itself with *+0*<sub>𝔽</sub> where the text takes ℝ of it, in the sort order's two conditions ("if _sortCompare_(old[_j_], old[_k_]) < *+0*<sub>𝔽</sub>", "… = *+0*<sub>𝔽</sub>") and in the definition of a consistent comparator ("_a_ <<sub>C</sub> _b_ means _comparator_(_a_, _b_) < *+0*<sub>𝔽</sub>", likewise for =<sub>C</sub> and ><sub>C</sub>).

1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"exponentiate"*, _base_, _exponent_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return _base_ raised to the power _exponent_.

1. If _x_ is *0*<sub>ℤ</sub> or _y_ is *0*<sub>ℤ</sub>, return _x_.
        1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"leftShift"*, _x_, _y_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return _x_ × *2*<sub>ℤ</sub><sup>_y_</sup>.

1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"multiply"*, _x_, _y_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return _x_ × _y_.

1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"add"*, _x_, _y_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return _x_ + _y_.

1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"subtract"*, _x_, _y_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return _x_ - _y_.

1. If _bits_ = 0 or _bigint_ is *0*<sub>ℤ</sub>, return *0*<sub>ℤ</sub>.
        1. If _bigint_ > *0*<sub>ℤ</sub> and _bits_ ≥ 4 × (DecimalExponent(ℝ(_bigint_)) + 1), return _bigint_.
        1. If BigIntTooLarge(*"asUintN"*, _bigint_, ℤ(_bits_)) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return ℤ(ℝ(_bigint_) modulo 2<sup>_bits_</sup>).

notes: §6.1.6.2 says a BigInt "may be any size and is not limited to a particular bit-width", and BigInt::exponentiate, BigInt::leftShift, BigInt::multiply, BigInt::add, BigInt::subtract and BigInt.asUintN return their exact results whatever their size; every implementation has a maximum size and throws a *RangeError* past it (V8 at 2<sup>30</sup> bits). SpecTec checks BigIntTooLarge before forming the result (propagating `?` through binary operators, BigInt::signedRightShift, and `++`/`--`; docs/spec-issues/51-bigint-maximum-size.md).

        1. Return the String value that is made from _n_ copies of _string_ appended together.

1. If _fillString_ is not the empty String and StringTooLarge(_intMaxLength_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return StringPad(_string_, _intMaxLength_, _fillString_, _placement_).

1. If StringTooLarge(the length of _result_ + the length of _nextString_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Set _result_ to the string-concatenation of _result_ and _nextString_.

1. If StringTooLarge(the length of _leftString_ + the length of _rightString_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Return the string-concatenation of _leftString_ and _rightString_.

1. If _k_ > 0, then
          1. If StringTooLarge(the length of _result_ + the length of _separator_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
          1. Set _result_ to the string-concatenation of _result_ and _separator_.

1. If StringTooLarge(the length of _result_ + the length of _elementString_) is *true*, throw a *RangeError* exception.
        1. Set _result_ to the string-concatenation of _result_ and _elementString_.

notes: Even below §6.1.4's 2<sup>53</sup> - 1 ceiling, every engine enforces a smaller finite-memory maximum String length and throws a *RangeError* past it (V8 2<sup>28</sup> on 32-bit and 2<sup>29</sup> - 24 on 64-bit, SpiderMonkey 2<sup>30</sup> - 2, JavaScriptCore 2<sup>31</sup> - 1). SpecTec asks the host via StringTooLarge (answering *true* past 2<sup>28</sup> code units in Engine) and throws a *RangeError* (docs/spec-issues/54-string-maximum-length.md).

notes: §6.1.4 defines the String type as sequences of up to 2<sup>53</sup> - 1 16-bit elements, yet String.prototype.repeat (`"ab".repeat(2 ** 52)`), String.prototype.concat, `+`, and JoinIndexedProperties have no `> 2^53 - 1` length guard before forming their result. SpecTec checks StringTooLarge (`Host.ValueLaws.stringTooLarge`, answering *true* past 2<sup>28</sup> and therefore past 2<sup>53</sup> - 1 in Engine) and throws a *RangeError* (docs/spec-issues/53-string-length-overflow.md).

§21.4.1.1 defines a finite time value first as an integral Number and then states a ±8.64 × 10<sup>15</sup> ms range. On `Date.UTC(275761, 0, -256)`, 1 January 275761 exceeds 8.64 × 10<sup>15</sup> ms while the resulting date is in range; SpecTec (@sec-makeday and @sort-time-value) bakes in reading "finite time value" as any finite integral Number, matching V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore (docs/spec-issues/10-utc-large-local-time.md).

ObjectLiteral's duplicate-`__proto__` early-error rule calls PropertyNameList -> PropName on every PropertyDefinition, including CoverInitializedName (`({a = 1})`), which has no PropName row in §8.6.5. SpecTec bakes in @row-propname-coverinitializedname, @formal-protopropertycount, and bottom-up child early-error short-circuiting so evaluation never stops with sortError (docs/spec-issues/29-propname-coverinitializedname.md).

Step 2.d.i's Assert follows `_receiver_.[[GetOwnProperty]](_propertyKey_)` returning *undefined*, which fails both when a Proxy receiver's trap hides a configurable target property and when an ordinary `_receiver_` inherits `_propertyKey_` from its prototype. SpecTec silences step 2.d.i via `assert pass` in S10.spectec:190 (docs/spec-issues/38-ordinaryset-receiver-has-property.md).

When a cover fails its "must cover" rule (`([...x = []]) => {}`, `async (...x = []) => {}`), unordered sibling and ancestor early-error rules still ask for "the |n| that is covered by _p_" — a Parse Node that does not exist. SpecTec (@formal-earlyerrorsof and LinEarly.linOwn) short-circuits children before parents and runs `must_cover` rules before other rules at each node (docs/spec-issues/39-must-cover-other-rules.md).

In §22.2.1's formal grammar, RegExpUnicodeEscapeSequence[+UnicodeMode] has both `u HexLeadSurrogate \u HexTrailSurrogate` and unguarded `u HexLeadSurrogate` alongside `u HexTrailSurrogate`, leaving `/\uD800\uDC00+/u`, `/[\uD800\uDC00]/u` and `/(?<\uD835\uDC9C>a)/` context-free ambiguous. SpecTec attaches a 16-prefix `[lookahead not_in { "\uDC", … }]` override in grammar-meta.txt and 04-grammar-regexp.spectec so greedy surrogate pairing is unambiguous and ParseLaws.complete holds (docs/spec-issues/55-regexp-unicode-escape-lookahead.md).

Before ASI inserts `;` after `let a` or `do {} while (false)`, no |RegularExpressionLiteral| is syntactically permitted, so literal §12 scans `/` on the next line as `DivPunctuator` and never re-lexes it after inserting `;` — rejecting `let a\n/x/.test("x")`! §12 also omits initial lexical goals for non-Script/Module ParseText calls. SpecTec (GoalsAt and NextASI in 04-derives.spectec) probes offending tokens under InputElementDiv and re-scans post-ASI tokens under their post-`;` syntactic context, using InputElementHashbangOrRegExp only at index 0 of |Script| or |Module| (docs/spec-issues/56-post-asi-lexical-goal.md).

In `ForStatement : for ( LexicalDeclaration Expression? ; Expression? ) Statement`, the first header `;` belongs to the child |LexicalDeclaration| rather than |ForStatement|; §5.1.5's declarative ASI also leaves `a = b\n+c` ambiguous; and §5.1.6.7 leaves `[no LineTerminator here]` inside lookahead sets undefined. SpecTec (04-derives.spectec) bans virtual `;` at the end of a `for`-header LexicalDeclaration (`ForHeadersExplicit`), formalizes left-to-right maximal viable prefix ASI (`ValidASI`), and adds `LookItem.noLT` (docs/spec-issues/57-asi-for-lexical-header.md).

§5.1.5 and §12.10 define ASI only for |Script| and |Module|, without stating that virtual semicolons inserted inside a cover _p_ (such as `(function () { let a\n return 1 })()`) survive when _p_ is reparsed as _n_. SpecTec's GrammarCtx.CoverIs (06-node-rel.spectec) and Ecma.reparse (Ops/Parse.lean, Relabel.lean) preserve virtual semicolons inside reparsed covers (docs/spec-issues/58-cover-reparse-virtual-semicolons.md).

Step 13.a exits only when `_lastIndex_ > _length_`, so at `_lastIndex_ = _length_` (reached on `""`, `/$/`, and the exhaustion step of every `/g` match) step 13.b asks for non-existent `element _lastIndex_ of _string_` in both BMP and Unicode modes. SpecTec's `@ph-input-index-of` (Helpers.spectec:78-89) returns `$ListLen(_input_)` when `_lastIndex_ == _length_` (docs/spec-issues/59-regexp-exec-end-of-string.md).

All three Annex B.3.2 replacement algorithms (`FunctionDeclarationInstantiation`, `GlobalDeclarationInstantiation`, `EvalDeclarationInstantiation`) run in place of |FunctionDeclaration| Evaluation and end with `Return ~unused~` instead of `Return ~empty~`, which would leak `~unused~` out of `eval("{ function f() {} }")` and overwrite prior statement values. SpecTec (S15.spectec:831-837) discards the closure's normal `~unused~` result and returns `~empty~` (docs/spec-issues/60-annexb-function-eval-empty.md).

Substituting |QuantifiableAssertion| for |Atom| in `Term :: Atom Quantifier` calls 2-argument `CompileAtom(_regexpRecord_, _direction_)`, which has no row for |QuantifiableAssertion| (whose semantics in §B.1.2.6 is 1-argument `CompileAssertion(_regexpRecord_)`). SpecTec adds `@row-compilesubpattern-quantifiableassertion-quantifier` in Helpers.spectec calling 1-argument `CompileAssertion` (docs/spec-issues/61-annexb-quantifiable-assertion.md).

§B.1.2.2 extends step 2 of CountLeftCapturingParensWithin to count `ExtendedAtom` groups, but leaves step 1 asserting `#sec-patterns`, which fails on every quantified §B.1.2 `ExtendedAtom` or `QuantifiableAssertion` (`#sec-regular-expressions-patterns`). SpecTec includes all 36 Annex B RegExp productions in `clause_prods @sec-patterns` (00-decls.spectec) and dispatches ParsePattern and CompileToCharSet under §B.1.2 (docs/spec-issues/62-annexb-capturing-parens-assert.md).

§B.3.2 tests "Early Errors for _func_" on a Function Object `_func_` and "_code_ Contains _x_" on a Parse Node `_x_`; §B.3.3 speaks of a "synthetic |BlockStatement|" with no AST or SDO rules; and §B.1.1 extends MultiLineComment with optional `HTMLCloseComment?`, making `/*a\nb*/` ambiguous. SpecTec reparses spliced `"var " + F + ";"` on the root source, widens Contains to Parse Node identity, splices `{` `}` for B.3.3 via `$CoveredBy(|IfStatement|, node)` (including in `LinEarly.linTree`), and existentially quantifies trivia trees (docs/spec-issues/63-annexb-replacing-and-b33.md).

CallMemberExpression and AwaitExpression use "covered by" with no "must cover" rule anywhere in ECMA-262, and Keyed/IteratorDestructuringAssignmentEvaluation ask for the |AssignmentPattern| covered by |DestructuringAssignmentTarget| whereas §13.15.5 puts the "must cover" rule on its child |LeftHandSideExpression|. SpecTec's `$CoveredBy` (`Ecma.reparse` in Ops/Parse.lean) reparses on demand whenever `(n, k)` was not cached by `must_cover` (docs/spec-issues/64-supplemental-covered-by.md).

§21.4.1.32 permits both 4-digit `YYYY` and expanded `+00YYYY` for years in `0..9999`, whereas test262 and all engines require 4-digit `YYYY` for `0..9999`. SpecTec adds `$ExpandedYearForm` in S21.spectec and binds it to `false` in Engine/Host/Core.lean (docs/spec-issues/65-toisostring-year-form.md).

Both algorithms pass a single mutable List (`_exportStarSet_` / `_resolveSet_`) across sibling `export *` branches without popping or copying, so any cycle-free diamond `export *` DAG (`a -> {b, c} -> d`) falsifies both circularity Asserts. SpecTec silences both via `assert pass` in S16.spectec:528, 563 (docs/spec-issues/66-module-diamond-circularity-asserts.md).

Unequal overlapping RMWs (`[0,2)` and `[0,4)`) are not ordered by §29.6.5 synchronizes-with (which requires equal ranges), allowing a 2-cycle in reads-bytes-from where ValueOfReadEvent ↔ ComposeWriteEventBytes diverges infinitely; §29.7.5 also leaves reads-bytes-from unquantified (since PR #3321), and §29.5.3 HostEventSet includes Synchronize events against §29.6.4. SpecTec (07-memory-model.spectec) defines ValueOf/Compose as an inductive least fixpoint, existentially quantifies `rbf`, converts Tear Free Reads' Assert to a conjunct, and defines HostSync over `inHost` (docs/spec-issues/67-memory-model-rmw-cycle.md).

SpecTec bakes in four prose/signature fixes: Cell.Emptied (25-host-laws-changes.spectec) empties *all* matching FinalizationRegistry cells rather than step 1.b's single `_cell_` per registry; $SuspendAgentUntil matches NotifyWaiter's Waiter Record parameter rather than `_thisAgent_` (#3328); $CanonicalPropertyValue selects UCD PropertyValueAliases.txt field 3 instead of a nonexistent "Canonical property value" column; and 00-decls.spectec declares `super [#"Module Record"]` on `#"Synthetic Module Record"` and models Private Name's `[[Description]]` as a Record field (docs/spec-issues/68-weakref-cells-and-unicode-sorts.md).
